coaching.title: What is Coaching?
coaching.description: The word 'Coach' might suggest instruction or advice, but the core spirit of professional coaching is quite the opposite. It is not top-down direction, but an equal 'partnership of exploration.' This relationship aims to empower you to find strength and answers from within.
coaching.hiking_metaphor_desc: A coach is like a 'hiking guide'. The guide knows the terrain and can point out potential paths and landscapes, but ultimately, 'the hiker decides which path to take'. The coach's role is to accompany you, helping you see your own strength, supporting your journey, not controlling it.

principles.title: Partner, Not Expert
principles.desc: The coach is your 'partner in exploration', not an expert providing all the answers. We believe everyone has innate potential for self-growth and problem-solving, and the coach's job is to help you uncover that potential.

principles.title: Listening & Questioning
principles.desc: The coach won't give advice or instruction. Instead, through deep listening and curious questioning, the coach creates a safe, non-judgmental space for you to discover your own solutions.

principles.title: Sparking Commitment
principles.desc: The aim of coaching conversations is to 'spark commitment'. Through dialogue, we explore possibilities together, and you decide which of them to turn into a concrete plan of action.

coaching.distinction_1_desc: Counseling and therapy address mental health and may involve assessment and treatment. Coaching does not diagnose or treat; it helps you explore where you want to go, make your own choices and act on them. When it would help, your coach will suggest seeing a mental health professional.
coaching.distinction_2_desc: Provides expert answers and diagnosis vs Coaching believes clients have their own answers.
coaching.distinction_3_desc: Senior guiding junior based on experience vs Coaching is a partnership without assumptions.
coaching.target_audience_desc: Whether you are facing doubts or obstacles in Career, Family, Life Direction, or Pursuing Dreams, coaching can support you. Suitable partners typically possess the following traits:

target_audience_list.title: Those willing to take responsibility for choices & actions
target_audience_list.desc: A core coaching mindset is acknowledging that clients are responsible for their own choices. Suitable clients don't expect the coach to give orders or answers, but are willing to make their own decisions with guidance and support.

target_audience_list.title: Those seeking clarity & removing 'noise'
target_audience_list.desc: For those who feel overwhelmed by overthinking. Coaching helps find focus, reprioritize goals, and find momentum when goals feel too open-ended.

target_audience_list.title: Those desiring self-transformation & 'becoming' better
target_audience_list.desc: Coaching isn't just about achieving goals, but who you become in the process. For those seeking self-awareness, challenging blind spots, and meaningful change.

target_audience_list.title: Those in a time of transition or challenge
target_audience_list.desc: Whether your life or work is changing, you face a new challenge, or you want to find your own pace again, coaching conversations help you take stock and see your direction more clearly.

target_audience_list.title: Those wanting to enhance leadership or relationships
target_audience_list.desc: Helping professionals navigate complex dynamics, improve leadership effectiveness, and handle difficult conversations involving both emotion and logic.

target_audience_list.title: People facing an important decision who want greater clarity
target_audience_list.desc: Whether it is a career pivot, a relationship choice, or a values-level crossroads, coaching helps you slow down, examine your assumptions, and make a decision you can own with confidence.

coaching.climber_metaphor_desc: People seeking a coach are like climbers preparing for a new path. They don't want someone to carry their backpack or carry them to the summit. They want a guide who knows the terrain to point out paths, but ultimately, the climber retains the decision of which way to go, building strength along the way.
coaching.card_principles_desc: Coaches are partners, not experts. We listen deeply and ask questions. The ultimate goal is to inspire your own commitment to action.

about.icf_desc: The ICF sets rigorous standards for the global coaching profession. Advancing from ACC to PCC involves not just accumulated hours, but a continuous refinement of the 'Coaching Mindset', 'Maintains Presence', and 'Deep Listening'.

credentials.acc: ACC (Associate Certified Coach): Entry level, requiring 60+ training hours and 100+ experience hours. All three coaches are working towards it now.
credentials.pcc: PCC (Professional Certified Coach): Professional level, requiring 125+ training hours and 500+ experience hours (the goal after ACC).
credentials.mindset: Coaching Mindset: The coach is a partner, not an expert. We believe clients have the potential for self-growth and problem-solving.

services.title: Services & Process
services.philosophy: Our coaching practice is built on trust, respect, and a deep belief in your capacity for growth. We stand as your partners in exploration, genuinely believing in your potential. Our goal is to guide and support you with an open, curious, and client-centered mindset, helping you discover your own solutions.

agreement_items.title: Recording & Consent
agreement_items.desc: For the ICF core competency assessment in the coach's ACC application, sessions are recorded, and may be transcribed, only if you agree. It's your choice: you can decline and still have your session.

agreement_items.title: Strict Confidentiality
agreement_items.desc: We follow the ICF Code of Ethics and keep your conversations strictly confidential. Apart from recordings and transcripts you agree to for the coach's ICF credential review, nothing is shared with any third party. Your privacy and trust matter deeply to us. Under the ICF Code of Ethics, confidentiality does not cover illegal activity, disclosure required by law, or imminent danger to you or others.

agreement_items.title: Client Responsibility
agreement_items.desc: Throughout the coaching relationship, you remain responsible for your own choices and actions.

agreement_items.title: Scheduling & Attendance
agreement_items.desc: Sessions are mainly online and scheduled by mutual agreement. Please give at least 24 hours notice for cancellations. Consistent attendance is key to progress.

agreement_items.title: Scope of Coaching
agreement_items.desc: Coaching is a forward-focused, action-oriented partnership. It is not therapy or counseling. If deeper mental health support is needed, your coach will refer you to the right professional.

faq_items.q: Which video app do you use?
faq_items.a: It depends on the coach, usually Google Meet or Zoom. Once the time is set, your coach sends you the meeting link.
Sessions are mainly online. If you would rather meet in person, talk it over with your coach.

faq_items.q: How do I give the coffee, drink or book?
faq_items.a: It's up to you after the session, for example buying your coach a coffee or a drink, or sending a book. There is no set amount.

faq_items.q: Do I have to continue after the first session?
faq_items.a: No. The first session comes with no commitment. If it feels right, you and your coach can decide whether to continue, usually for about 3 to 6 sessions.

faq_items.q: Is what I share kept confidential?
faq_items.a: Yes. We follow the ICF Code of Ethics. For the coach's ICF credential review, sessions are recorded, and may be transcribed, only with your consent, and used only for that review; beyond that, nothing you share goes to any third party. You can decline recording and still have your session. Under the ICF Code of Ethics, confidentiality does not cover illegal activity, disclosure required by law, or imminent danger to you or others.

faq_items.q: How is coaching different from counseling?
faq_items.a: Coaching is a forward-focused partnership. Through listening and questions, your coach helps you clarify your goals, find your own answers and act on them. It is not therapy or counseling; if you need deeper mental health support, your coach will help refer you to the right professional.

faq_items.q: Can I book without a clear goal?
faq_items.a: Yes. Many people start knowing only that there is something they want to think through, or that they feel stuck. The first session can start from where things are now, and you and your coach work out together what you want to focus on.

process_steps.title: Discovery Session
process_steps.desc: The first session to establish the 'Coaching Agreement', clarifying 'Where you want to go' and 'What you hope to achieve'.

process_steps.title: Regular Sessions
process_steps.desc: Approx. 3 to 6 one-on-one sessions, mainly online, 45 mins each. Deep exploration and progress tracking.

process_steps.title: Transformation & Action
process_steps.desc: Turning what you explore into an action plan you choose, committing to it and getting started.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: We care about your privacy. This page explains what information we receive when you use this site and book a session, how we use it, and how you can see or delete it.

sections.title: Site analytics
sections.body: We use Cloudflare Web Analytics to see how many people visit and which pages help. It uses no cookies and does not track individuals; we only see anonymous totals such as page views, country and device type.

sections.title: Outside services
sections.body: Fonts come from Google Fonts and the analytics script from Cloudflare. When a page loads, your browser connects to their servers.

sections.title: Settings kept in your browser
sections.body: Your language and light or dark mode choice are stored only in your own browser and never sent to us.

sections.title: Booking form
sections.body: Booking uses Google Forms, so your answers are stored by Google. Isaac, one of our coaches, receives the form and passes only what is needed to arrange the session to the coach you chose. We use this information only to arrange and contact you about sessions, and do not share it with any other third party.

sections.title: Session content
sections.body: What you share in sessions is kept confidential. For the coach's ICF credential review, sessions are recorded, and may be transcribed, only with your consent; these are used only for that review. You can decline recording and still have your session. Under the ICF Code of Ethics, confidentiality does not cover illegal activity, disclosure required by law, or imminent danger to you or others.

sections.title: Emailing a coach directly
sections.body: If you email a coach directly, only that coach receives it; it is stored by the coach's email provider (such as Gmail) and used only to answer you.

sections.title: Keeping and deleting
sections.body: We keep your information only as long as it is needed. You can email us at any time to see, correct or delete it.
